_purpose: Single source of truth for which data each fit uses. Every script reads this file. All partitions below are RESERVED for the human baseline (Reddit, HN) or the agent baseline (Moltbook) and must never be reused for agent conditioning.

hn.note: BigQuery bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full not configured in this environment (no credentials); using the brief's Hugging Face fallback.

moltbook_crawl.note: SQLite crawl, observation 2026-01-27..2026-02-09. Stores at most 100 comments per post (API limit; 10,728 posts affected per README). Contains the ~42 h comment outage starting 2026-02-01.

reddit.thread_window_applies_to: submission created_utc (root). All comments on in-window submissions are kept, including those after the window end, so reply delays are not truncated at 2021-12-31.

proxy_c_subreddits.use_restriction: These subreddits are used only for the position check (Step 4, proxy c). Reserved for the human baseline like all other partitions; never reused for agent conditioning.
proxy_c_subreddits.pre_use_checks: S10 bot review (authors in >1% of threads, by hand) and deletion/removal rates reported before any use.
proxy_c_subreddits.contest_mode_effects: Per Reddit's API description as reproduced in PRAW 7.7.1 SubmissionModeration.contest_mode: comment thread defaults to random sort; replies to top-level comments are hidden behind '[show replies]'; scores hidden from non-moderators (obscured to 1 via the API).
proxy_c_subreddits.event_restriction: Proxy (c) uses only replies whose parent is a top-level comment (depth-2 comments): top-level comments are the only items shown in randomized order; deeper comments are collapsed by default. Applied to AskHistorians random-sort threads too, for comparability (random sort does not collapse replies).

proxy_d.note: within the two study subreddits only (decision after step 2)

reddit.processing: one subreddit at a time: data/processed/reddit/<subreddit>/items.parquet and split.parquet

hn.thread_window_applies_to: story/poll time (root). All descendants kept regardless of their own time.

post_classes.link: story with non-empty url, not Ask/Show HN
post_classes.text_other: story without url, not Ask/Show HN (Tell HN, Launch HN, etc.)
post_classes.deleted_root: story/poll with deleted=true (no title/url, cannot be classified); reported as its own class from step 2 on

moltbook.thread_window_applies_to: post created_at (root). All comments on in-window posts are kept.
moltbook.gap_note: Periodicity-sensitive analyses must use contiguous segments. The 41.7 h gap is the 2026-02-01 commenting outage documented in the moltbook-crawl README; located empirically in step 1 (outputs/moltbook*/step1_coverage_gaps.csv).
moltbook.archive_role: SimulaMet archive is a cross-check only, and only for posts created 2026-02-08 onward (decision after step 1).
moltbook.segment_use: Steps 3 and 6 (timing, hazards, tails) use only the two contiguous segments. Step 2 structure uses the whole thread window.

truncation.thread_size: API-reported comment_count from the post table (complete for all posts).
truncation.shape_statistics: depth, fan-out by depth, reciprocity, OP return, bimodality use only completely stored threads (stored comments >= API-reported comment_count). Reddit and HN are reported both full-population and size-matched (threads with < 100 comments), side by side.
truncation.fits: stored size is right-censored at 100 in any fit that uses the trees.

spam_filter.source: De Marzo & Garcia (2026), Collective Behavior of AI Agents: the Case of Moltbook
spam_filter.rule: for posts with >= 5 stored comments, exclude the post if unique comment content / stored comments < 0.5 or unique comment authors / stored comments < 0.2
spam_filter.applies_to: all Moltbook analyses from step 2 on

archive_crosscheck.note: archive cross-check only (decision after step 1); split by the same hash rule with dataset key 'moltbook_archive'; used in step 4b speed reconciliation

holdout.stratify_by: calendar month (UTC) of root creation, per dataset (Reddit additionally per subreddit, HN additionally per post class)
holdout.method: within each stratum, threads are ranked by sha256('<seed>:<dataset>:<thread_id>') and the lowest round(0.2 * n) are assigned to validation; deterministic, no RNG state
holdout.assignment_files: data/processed/<dataset>/split.parquet (regenerable from this file; per-stratum counts in outputs/<dataset>/step1_split_counts.csv)

inner_calibration_fold.purpose: model selection by held-out likelihood inside the calibration split (step 3 on); the 20% validation split is never used for fitting or selection

quantity_lists.rule: No quantity appears on both lists. Reply half-life is calibration only.

author_filters.bot_name_rule: case-insensitive regex (^bot[_-]|[_-]bot$|bot$) on Reddit author names: SENSITIVITY ONLY, never a filter
author_filters.top_active_definition: authors ranked by comment count within the dataset's in-window threads (per subreddit for Reddit); ties broken by name
author_filters.application: Filters are applied at comment level in analyses (comment excluded as a reply / parent candidate), not at tree-building time, so trees stay intact.
author_filters.primary_filter: explicit list in config/reddit_bot_authors.txt (AutoModerator, eliassjogreen/Reddit-Bot-List, known utility bots)

position_proxies.a: confidence-sort position from final score; look-ahead-affected (Reddit only). Reported with ties broken oldest-first and at random; dropped for a subreddit if the two disagree materially (step4b.proxy_a_ties). Step 4b: no material disagreement in philosophy or buildapc, kept for both
position_proxies.b: early-thread arrival order, first 30 minutes; MAIN identification
position_proxies.c: contest-mode threads (order randomized). PLACEBO CHECK ONLY (decision after the audit): no further contest-mode data
position_proxies.d: suggested_sort = 'new' threads; second arrival-order identification (display order = reverse arrival)
position_proxies.hn: HN comment scores are hidden and its sort uses them, so HN position is latent: use only proxy (b) on HN

descriptive_scope.step2: Descriptive statistics are computed on the CALIBRATION split only; validation threads are left untouched for model validation.

step3.fit_cap_method: if the fit fold has more parent comments, keep those with sha256('<seed>:cap:<id>') in the lowest 2,000,000
step3.events: first direct reply that is not a self-reply and not by an explicit-list bot, created before the parent's censoring time

censoring.moltbook: thread's last crawl time (max crawled_at in the thread); comments created in contiguous segment 1 are also censored at the segment end (comment outage start)

moltbook_threads.primary: complete (stored >= API-reported), non-spam, calibration split; parent comments created in one of the two contiguous segments
moltbook_threads.sensitivity: adds incomplete non-spam threads, each censored at the creation time of its last stored comment (assumes the stored comments are the earliest; the API's selection rule is undocumented, see reports/step2b.md)

age_fe.cap_method: threads in calibration split ordered by sha256('<seed>:4b:<thread_id>'), taken until the parent count would exceed the cap

proxy_a_ties.material_disagreement: |beta_random - beta_oldest| > max(0.05, 2 x thread-clustered SE) or |flattening difference| > 0.01 or the flattening CIs fall on opposite sides of 0; if material, proxy (a) is dropped for that subreddit

position_b.rank: arrival rank among siblings created in the first 30 min of the thread; parents with >= 2 such siblings
controls: depth dummies (only those with >= 10 first-reply events)
position_b.placebo: r/Fantasy contest-mode threads, top-level comments; control: r/Fantasy non-contest threads with >= 20 comments

step5.cap_method: roots ordered by sha256('<seed>:4b:<thread_id>'), first cap_roots kept
step5.events: top-level comments: visible (not dead), not by the root author, not explicit-list bots
step5.candidate_answer: first such top-level comment (never defined by score)

step6.bin_edges: 0, then 40 log-spaced edges from 10 s to 30 d

dose_response.states: number of earlier top-level comments: 0, 1, 2, >=3; each event belongs to the state it ends
dose_response.covariates: step_1 = 1[>=1 earlier], step_2 = 1[>=2], step_3 = 1[>=3]; thread FE; root-age bins as step5

show_hn_control.population: hn show_hn, all calibration live roots

placebo.base_shape: log-normal density in root age, median 7200 s, sigma 1.5 (log seconds)
placebo.rate: lambda_g(t) = A_P * a_g * base(t) * [1 + (M - 1) * 1(spike_g and T_g <= t < T_g + D)]
placebo.matching: for each (pi, M) and population P, (A_P, k_P) chosen so that the simulated mean top-level comments per root within 3 d and the share of roots with >= 1 match the Step 5 calibration values (ask_hn 6.424, 0.736; link 1.755, 0.236)
placebo.estimator: scripts/step5_saturation.py cells + FEPoissonBoot, raw weights, unchanged

sweepers.population: moltbook_crawl complete, non-spam, outage handled (step6 default), roots
sweepers.bump_statistic: R = observed events in bins with midpoints in [1 d, 2 d] / expected from a Poisson log-log linear fit on bins with midpoints in [0.25 d, 0.9 d] and [2.2 d, 6 d]; per-author primary, raw also; thread bootstrap B = 200
sweepers.disappears: bump present with the sweepers' replies and, without them, R's 95% CI includes 1 or lies below 1

archive_late_authors.population: moltbook_archive cross-check window, roots and comments, default events
archive_late_authors.late: reply delay > 3 d (the step6 tail window, up to 30 d)
statistics: authors of replies in spike bins: 3-30 d bins whose events exceed 2x the fitted 3-30 d power law
archive_late_authors.intervals: thread bootstrap B = 200 for shares and HHI
